newsitem.title: USA: US spot natgas prices up on weather, stock refills.
newsitem.headline: US spot natgas prices up on weather, stock refills.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices extended last week's late gains Monday with the help of cooler temperatures in the East, firmer futures and storage buying in the producing region, market sources said.
Louisiana Gulf Coast prices rose nearly five cents to about $1.90 per mmBtu, with Henry Hub quoted mostly in the mid-$1.90s.
In south Texas, buyers took advantage of above-normal temperatures by injecting more gas into storage, pushing prices about four cents higher into the low-to-mid $1.80s.
Earlier in the NYMEX session, April Henry Hub natgas futures soared to a high of $2.04, up 9.3 cents from Friday. However, this afternoon the contract retreated into the low-$1.90s.
In the East, New York city-gate prices climbed into the low-to-mid $2.20s, up about 10 cents, as cooler-than-normal weather was forecast for the region this week.
Similarly in the Appalachian region prices edged up three cents to about $2.
In the Midcontinent, prices rose by about two cents to the high-$1.70s, with Demarcation quoted mostly in the low-$1.80s.
Temperatures in the Midwest are expected to run near to slightly above normal through the end of the week.
In the Permian basin, gas prices firmed more than five cents to the high-$1.70s, while the Waha market jumped to $1.80-1.85.
Southern California border prices were quoted mostly in the mid-$1.80s.

The restart of the 1,070 megawatt San Onofre 2 nuclear unit in southern California will likely be delayed again to a new date of March 20 following repairs of a leak, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission said in its Monday status report.
